To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

bilinguals do not experience immediate cross language competition when reading sentences that bias the English meaning of interlingually ambiguous homographs, but do experience competition later when the sentence context biases the Spanish meaning of the same homographs.
bilinguals do not experience immediate cross-language interference during the processing of interlingual words in context.

(1) bilingual readers are not always subject to cross-lingual competition, but rather dynamically adapt to contextual language cues, and (2) the time course of this adaptation is influenced by the degree of language dominance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how bilinguals read and understand text.
the cognitive processes underlying language comprehension in bilinguals.
the nature and time course of interlingual interference and facilitation during reading and the factors that influence the emergence of these effects.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
bilinguals do not always experience cross language competition.
bilinguals are able to dynamically adapt their lexical access to the context of a given situation.
the bilingual brain is not only a bilingual brain, but also a monolingual brain, depending on context.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the bilingual lexicon is dynamic and that it can be selectively activated in a language appropriate manner.

the bilinguals are not always experiencing cross language interference, but rather they are dynamically adapting to context and selectively access the information associated with the cued language under specific conditions.
bilinguals are able to adaptively access their lexicon based on context.
The main takeaway from our work is that
bilinguals are not necessarily always competing between their two languages.
eye tracking can be used to study bilingual word recognition.
the processing of interlingual words is not a simple competition between the two languages.
